text.title: Growth Viral Loops Worked Example
text.summary: One complete viral-loop spec for a collaborative whiteboard (board_shared as the inherent loop, K 0.648 from 1.8 invites per user x 0.36 accept rate over three cycles, 6-day cycle, 1,000 to 2,838 users in 90 days ignoring churn, target 0.8 as an increment against a 0.05-0.20 benchmark, three-step invitee path with two friction experiments, five joinable events, invitee D30 0.41 vs organic 0.38, no incentive) with a note on each value, plus a bolt-on referral page written up as a viral loop and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A collaborative whiteboard product: users share boards with colleagues to get work done, and some of those colleagues become users. Every invite carries an invite_id and the inviter's user_id. Over the last three loop cycles active users sent 1.8 invites each and 36 percent of invites turned into accounts; the median invitee sends their own first invite 6 days after receiving one. Nothing is paid for referrals. The team wants a spec with a defensible K target and the experiments most likely to move it.

example.title: board collaboration loop
example.note: `board_shared` is the moment the inviter needs a collaborator to finish their own work, so the loop fires on every board rather than once after signup, and no invite modal is listed as the primary loop (r-share-moment-is-inherent). K = 1.8 invites per active user x 0.36 accepts per invite = 0.648, each component with its 30-day window and sample, measured over three cycles (r-k-factor-decomposed). Cycle time is the median of 4,100 send-to-first-send pairs, 6 days; `project(1000, 0.648, 6, 90)` in templates/loop-projection.py returns 2,838, and the spec says the model ignores churn (r-cycle-time-measured-and-projected). Current K is above 0.4 so a self-sustaining target would be permitted, but the team targets 0.8 as an increment because the B2B SaaS benchmark is 0.05 to 0.20 and 0.648 is already far above it (r-k-target-anchored-to-baseline). The invitee path is three steps; the accept rate 0.36 is open link 0.62 x create account 0.58, and the rank-one experiment removes the email verification gate at the weakest step, naming the conversion it expects to move (r-friction-steps-capped). All five events carry invite_id and inviter_user_id so K and cycle time come from joined rows; invitee D30 0.41 is reported next to organic 0.38 (r-loop-events-instrumented). No reward is paid, so `incentive` is null and `compensation_disclosure` is not_applicable; recipients are addresses the inviter types in, with CASL consent and a GDPR basis recorded (r-referral-consent-and-disclosure).

example.title: a referral page written up as a viral loop
example.note: What the validator prints: `primary_loop.share_event` invite_modal_shown is a bolt-on surface and `kind` is not inherent (r-share-moment-is-inherent); K components are 0 with a sample of 1 while `k` is 0.7, and `cycles_measured` 1 is below 2 (r-k-factor-decomposed); `cycle_time.method` estimated and `projection.ignores_churn` false (r-cycle-time-measured-and-projected); `target_k` 1.2 as self_sustaining from `current_k` 0.15, benchmark source too short (r-k-target-anchored-to-baseline); five steps in `invitee_path` where three is the cap, an experiment on a step that is not in the path with no expected lift (r-friction-steps-capped); two events instead of five, keyed on user_id without invite_id (r-loop-events-instrumented); `incentive.trigger_milestone` signup_completed, `self_referral_block` with only ip, `excludes_existing_and_past_users` false (r-reward-on-activation-not-signup); `recipient_source` contact import without consent, `casl_express_consent` false, and a paid referral with `compensation_disclosure` not_applicable (r-referral-consent-and-disclosure). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: 0.7 is not 0 x 0, and 12,000 projected users is not what loop-projection.py returns for K 0.15.
